To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gonadotrophins stimulate VEGF production in granulosa cells and that VEGF may play a role in follicle development and ovulation.
the midcycle gonadotropinic surge stimulates VEGF production in the periovolutory follicle and that FSH and LH directly stimulate VEGFs production by granulosacells.

the ovulatory gonadotropic surge stimulates the production of VEGF by granulosa luteinized and nonluteinized cells, and that FSH-like and LH-like gonadotropic stimulation of VEGF production occurs in both nonluteinizing and luteinization granulosa cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanisms by which the midcycle gonadotropinic surge promotes the formation of the corpus luteum.
elucidating the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie the formation and function of the corpus luteum in the human and nonhuman primates.
the regulation of vascular endothelial cell growth factor (VEGFA) production by the granulosa cell during the periovular interval.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gonadotrophins (FSH or LH/CG), in addition to the ovulatory stimulus of the LH surge, are important regulators of VEGF production in the periovularly follicle.
the midcycle gonadotropinic surge stimulates VEGF production in granulosa cells, thereby providing the necessary stimulus to initiate neovascularization and the formation of the corpus luteum.
gonadotrophin (LH and/or FSH) surge stimulates the synthesis of vascular endothelial cell growth factor (VEGFF) by granulosa cell in the ovulatory (preovulatory) follicles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the midcycle gonadotropic surge is a critical regulator of VEGF production in the periovolutory follicle, which may be important for the establishment of the neovascular network in the newly formed corpus luteum.
the midcycle surge in gonadotropinin primate females promotes the synthesis and secretion of VEGF by granulosa cell of the periovulatory (i.e. luteinizing) follicle.

the midcycle gonadotropic surge stimulates VEGF production in the periovulating follicle, and the FSH-like and LH-like components of the gonadotropinic surge act directly on the granulosa cells of preovulatory follicle to stimulate VEGF production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VEGF is a product of luteinizing cells and that it is stimulated by gonadotropinic hormones, which are the key regulators of the ovulatory process.
the midcycle gonadotropinin surge stimulates VEGF synthesis and secretion by granulosa cell in the preovulatory follicle.
gonadotrophins are important in the regulation of VEGF production in granulosa cells, and this is important for the neovascularisation of the corpus luteum.
